claude-s · archive-footage

Old film b-roll, licences checked at the source

grab 3 seconds each of a film countdown, a typewriter close-up and a 1950s city street from movingimagearchive.com. make sure they're actually public domain, then cut a quick 12 s test with the credits at the end

What the skill did

  • Three searches on movingimagearchive.com, picked by eye from the numbered contact sheets: a NASA countdown leader, a 1920s typewriter close-up and a 1955 downtown street.
  • MIA labels every source public domain and has no terms page, so each licence was re-read at the archive the film came from: images.nasa.gov and archive.org.
  • Credit: "The Time of Apollo - 1960 to 1975" (NASA KSC, 1960), NASA Image and Video Library. Public domain: a US federal work, NASA-credited at images-api.nasa.gov. https://images.nasa.gov/details/KSC-1960-to-1975-MH-NAS01-0001-The_Time_of_Apollo-B_2140
  • Credit: "Farmer Miller Goes Into High Gear (Part I)" (Goodyear Tire & Rubber Company, ca. 1920s), Prelinger Archives, Internet Archive. Public domain in the US: published before 1931; archive.org licenseurl is CC public domain. https://archive.org/details/FarmerMi1920
  • Credit: "Miracle on the Delaware" (WPTZ Motion Picture Unit, ca. 1955), Prelinger Archives, Internet Archive. Public domain by archive.org's licenseurl only, so the helper flags it: check renewal before commercial use. https://archive.org/details/Miracleo1955
  • --best swapped MIA's 320x240 copy of the typewriter film for archive.org's MPEG-2 original (640x480) after the frames lined up (r = 0.99).
  • Cut with ffmpeg at 960x720 (4:3, square pixels), a light film look at 0.3, and an end card rendered by archive.py credits --card.

Sound

  • A quiet projector-flutter bed synthesised with ffmpeg: brown noise, band-limited, 24 Hz tremolo, about -34 LUFS. No clip audio is used.
